sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][D153][F6][D192][F7][D232].
The FY2022 jump came primarily from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
Revenue then declined three straight years, by 16.5% in FY2023, 1.8% in FY2024 and 4.6% in FY2025 to $184 billion [F8][D274][F9][D316][F10][D358].
The FY2025 decline was mainly lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes and natural gas prices [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth as it fell 5.3% [D402][D404][D403].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, at 11.6% of revenue and +1.5pp of growth on a 16.5% increase [D418][D420][D419].
Worldwide net oil-equivalent production rose 12% in FY2025, primarily on the Hess acquisition and growth in TCO, the Permian and the Gulf of America [P28].
Operating costs grew 1.2pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 3.4% against a 4.6% revenue decline [D379][D373][D358].
Net income fell 30.5% while diluted EPS fell 31.8%, as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [D359][D361][D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, while SG&A rose to 2.7% from 2.4% [D338][D296][D340][D298].
Purchased crude oil and products decreased on lower crude and refined product prices and volumes, partly offset by higher natural gas prices and volumes [P14].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5%, and net margin of 6.7% sat 2.5pp below the prior year's level [D345][D303][F30][D369].
Operating cash flow of $33.9 billion was 2.76x net income, above the 1.97x window median [F60][D346][D644].
The FY2025 increase was primarily higher cash distributions from TCO and contributions from legacy Hess assets, more than offsetting lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow of $16.6 billion was 1.35x net income and an 8.8% margin, against a 13.4% peer median [F80][D347][D343][D634].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F70][D342][D348].
Cash and investments were $7.3 billion at FY2025, down 11.8% [D349][D375].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so total debt and net cash after that year are omitted from this pack [X193].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D353][D354].
Return on average equity was 7.3%, below the 14.9% peer median and in the 17th percentile of six peers [D357][D642][D641].
Revenue declined in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R1][F8][F9][F10].
Three years of falling revenue on lower realizations and margins is a cyclical squeeze, not yet a structural break, but it leaves little room for cost growth [R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 132.8%, 179.7% and 149.7% [R4][D270][D312][D354].
Payout above free cash flow is being funded from the balance sheet and asset sales, which is sustainable only while cash generation holds [R4].
Revenue for FY2018 through FY2025 in the table is a later recast, not the figure first reported; FY2025 is $184.4 billion against $189.0 billion in that year's 10-K [R3][F10][X10].
Growth and margins that compare a recast year with a year never recast mix two presentations, so the window CAGR should be read with that caveat [R3].
Whether net margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the 7.9% window median or falls toward the -5.9% FY2020 low [D613][D611].
Whether free cash flow margin in the FY2026 10-K recovers toward the 8.9% window median from 8.8% [D616][D343].
Whether buybacks plus dividends in the FY2026 10-K fall below the 149.7% of free cash flow reported for FY2025 [D354].
